## D4 - the source check judges it (FR-003)

decisions.summary: Category built as guideline rule, kind+subject marks, build refusal, source-applicability judgment; first use The Complete Servant (archive, independent check of 25 rows, comparative questions, answer on #2).
decisions.why: Restates FR-001..FR-007 and the GM's ruling (option 1); adds nothing.

decisions.id: TC-1 one write page session (three questions) then one check session
decisions.summary: Record edits in one write session and one check session.
decisions.why: Method only; carries FR-006.

decisions.id: TC-2 edition and page from the Internet Archive scan Gutenberg was made from
decisions.summary: Gutenberg text has no page numbers, so pages come from the IA scan named in the registry entry.
decisions.why: The means of meeting FR-007's edition-and-page clause and the asker's 'Note the edition and page of each figure'.

decisions.id: TC-3 'Where a page cannot be read on the scan, the answer says so'
decisions.summary: Fallback when a figure's page cannot be read on the scan.
decisions.why: Carve-out from FR-007 'MUST give the edition and page of each figure', but only for the case where giving the page is physically impossible (an unreadable page on the scan); it reports the gap rather than hiding it. It does not license skipping a readable page.

decisions.summary: No performance bookends; one set lookup per cited key.
decisions.why: No map or render work; no fidelity question.

decisions.summary: Principle mapping: questions research:physical, tooling research:rendering, coverage held.
decisions.why: Process conformance; narrows nothing asked.

decisions.id: D1 kind/section/subject/contents vocabulary and europe/elsewhere note
decisions.summary: Source kind 'comparative' (carried as PRIMARY), works section, question subject, questions section with limits in its description; europe/elsewhere explanations note the money-only yardstick use.
decisions.why: Carries FR-002 (marked where a reader meets them) and keeps the tags consistent with FR-001's limits.

decisions.id: D2 build refusal keyed on PRIMARY kind 'comparative'
decisions.summary: _works refuses a cited key whose PRIMARY kind is comparative on a question without subject comparative; test proves refusal, pass and chip.
decisions.why: FR-004 says 'A comparative source cited by a question that is not comparative MUST be caught' - not 'a source whose primary kind is comparative'. The vocabulary's own multi-value form (kind=comparative,primary, D1) admits 'comparative' as a NON-primary kind beside another (e.g. a scholarship work on Regency wages tagged kind=scholarship,primary;comparative). Such a work cited by a Rokugani question passes D2 unchecked - exactly the GM's limit ('not because we will use it to establish the actual value of a koku'). D1 states the convention that a comparative work carries the kind as primary, but no block enforces it. Not impossible, not implied by the GM, does not serve the purpose. Fix (either): D2 refuses a cited key carrying kind 'comparative' at ANY position; OR the vocabulary/build refuses 'comparative' as a non-primary kind (and the test proves that refusal too).

decisions.id: D2 question test on subject 'comparative' (not comparative+money)
decisions.summary: A question counts as comparative when its subjects include comparative.
decisions.why: Matches FR-004's wording 'a question that is not comparative'; D1 tags every comparative question comparative,money and FR-001's money-only limit lives in the guidelines.

decisions.id: D3 guidelines section in research/CLAUDE.md, pointer in money-requests.md, full text with GM verbatim in docs/research-record-rules.md
decisions.summary: What it is, why (GM's words), limits as FR-001 lists, how marked.
decisions.why: Carries FR-001 and the GM's 'update our research guidelines to indicate what this category is and why it exists, and also what the limits are'; all four FR-001 limits are listed.

decisions.id: D4 source-applicability judges comparative works on own-society soundness and stated limits, not East-Asia fit; NOT-APPLICABLE for misuse
decisions.summary: New paragraph in the contract; vocabulary block re-derived.
decisions.why: Carries FR-003 and the GM's ruling that the record takes the book as a comparative source. Note: it is keyed on PRIMARY kind like D2; the D2 fix (any-position or primary-only enforced) closes the same seam here.

decisions.id: D5 registry entry adams-1825-complete-servant with limits in write-ups; tags period/region/kind; make archive
decisions.summary: The source registered and archived.
decisions.why: Carries FR-005 'MUST be archived' and the asker's item 1 'archive the text'.

decisions.id: D6 extraction check verdict list READ / MISQUOTED / WRONG-POST / WRONG-SECTION / NOT-FOUND
decisions.summary: source-reader checks each of the 25 copied rows against the archived text with this closed verdict set, plus the housekeeper/house steward finding; reply kept as extraction/check.md.
decisions.why: The asker asked for 'each quote AND FIGURE against the text' (request, 'check gm-assistant's extraction - its 25 complete-servant servant-wage rows ... each quote and figure against the text'); FR-005 requires 'each discrepancy named'. The closed list has no slot for a row whose quote is verbatim but whose extracted wage figure disagrees with it (or with the text), and the block does not tell the reader to compare the figure field at all. A discrepancy the asker named explicitly can therefore go unreported or be mis-filed as MISQUOTED. Fix: add a WRONG-FIGURE verdict (the row's figure disagrees with its quote or the text) and state that each row's figure field is compared, not only its quote.

decisions.id: D6 rows copied from gm-assistant main into extraction/rows.jsonl with the commit
decisions.summary: Pins the 25 rows checked.
decisions.why: Carries FR-005's '25 at gm-assistant 9459638a'.

decisions.id: D7 three comparative questions, tagged subject=comparative,money; setting=city; level=counts-and-measurements; no drawing page; intro states yardstick
decisions.summary: Wages by post (from checked rows), income division and servants by income, provision prices verbatim with SILENT for unpriced items.
decisions.why: Carries FR-006's three bullets, FR-002's marking and the GM's 'openly comparative question ... what did a Regency English household pay its servants?'. FR-006 allows 'one or more' questions.

decisions.summary: Per question: fragment file, verdicts, what is open; extraction result per row; edition and page per figure.
decisions.why: Carries FR-007 and the asker's 'Same answer format: fragment files, verdicts, what is still open'.

decisions.summary: Vocabulary/build, guidelines/contract, source, extraction check, questions, implementation check, answer, done and land.
decisions.why: Sequencing only.

blocks: ## D2 - the build catches a misuse (FR-004)
## D4 - the source check judges it (FR-003)

decisions.summary: site.py is an engine file, so the landing is GATED
decisions.why: Process for landing; changes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: One write page session for the three questions, then one check session
decisions.why: How FR-006's questions are produced; no scope change.

decisions.summary: Edition and page of each figure are taken from the Internet Archive scan the Gutenberg text was made from (Gutenberg keeps no page numbers), named in the registry entry
decisions.why: Carries the request's 'Note the edition and page of each figure' and FR-007.

decisions.summary: Where a page cannot be read on the scan, the answer says so instead of giving the page
decisions.why: FR-007 and the request ask for the page of EACH figure; this carve-out covers only the case where the page is physically unreadable on the scan, where giving it is impossible, and it reports the gap openly in the answer rather than omitting it silently. It does not cover a page that is merely awkward to find.

decisions.summary: Performance bookends N/A: one set lookup per cited key
decisions.why: Cost statement only.

decisions.summary: Constitution check: no map or glyph; lint/coverage held; question tasks research: physical, tooling tasks research: rendering
decisions.why: Process classification; agrees with FR-008 (no map change).

decisions.summary: Source kind 'comparative' in source-tags.json, carried as a comparative work's primary kind
decisions.why: FR-002: marks the source where a reader meets it; its text restates FR-001's limits.

decisions.summary: Works section works-comparative before works-beyond-east-asia
decisions.why: FR-002: comparative works listed apart, under their own heading.

decisions.summary: Question subject 'comparative' and contents section comparative-money after money; comparative questions tagged subject=comparative,money
decisions.why: FR-002: marks the question; the section description states the category and its limits (FR-001).

decisions.summary: europe and elsewhere tag explanations add that, for money alone, such sources serve as a comparative yardstick, never the setting's own figures
decisions.why: Keeps the existing region explanations consistent with the GM's new category; restates FR-001's limits, adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: _works refuses a cited key carrying kind 'comparative' in ANY position on a question whose subjects lack 'comparative'; test covers comparative as first kind and as a later kind, the pass on a comparative question, and the chip on the built page
decisions.why: FR-004 exactly. Round 1's item (refusal limited to primary kind, a narrowing of FR-004) is closed: the check now fires on any position and the test proves the later-kind case. The test is enforcement of FR-004/SC-002, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: research/CLAUDE.md section defining the category (what, why in the GM's words, the four limits, how marked); money-requests.md points at it; full text with GM's words in docs/research-record-rules.md
decisions.why: FR-001 and the GM's 'update our research guidelines to indicate what this category is and why it exists, and also what the limits are'. All four FR-001 limits are listed.

decisions.summary: source-applicability judges a work carrying kind 'comparative' in any position on soundness as a record of its own society's money and on whether its write-up states the limits; not on East Asian fit; NOT-APPLICABLE when cited outside a comparative question or used as the basis of a Rokugani figure
decisions.why: FR-003. Round 1's item (primary kind only) is closed: any position now. Limits mapping: money-only -> 'cited outside a comparative question' (comparative questions are money questions); never cited for how a place was built/farmed/lived in -> same condition; never anything on a map -> same condition (a map is not a comparative money question); never a koku's value or a Rokugani price or wage -> 'used as the basis of a Rokugani figure'; not sought out unless the GM asks or approves -> a limit on seeking, carried by the guideline (D3) and stated in the write-up D4 checks for. The comparative purpose (a sound yardstick on its own society's money) is the first test.

decisions.summary: Registry entry adams-1825-complete-servant naming Gutenberg text and scan, write-ups stating the comparative limits, tags period=modern-preindustrial; region=europe; kind=comparative,primary; text archived
decisions.why: FR-005 (archive) and FR-002 (marked).

decisions.summary: The 25 complete-servant rows copied with their commit; a source-reader checks each row's QUOTE and FIGURE (wage, unit, period) against the archived text, verdicts READ / MISQUOTED / WRONG-FIGURE / WRONG-POST / WRONG-SECTION / NOT-FOUND with the passage; and whether any wage line names the housekeeper or house steward
decisions.why: FR-005 / SC-003 and the asker's 'each quote and figure against the text' and 'misquote, wrong post, or wage I attached to the wrong section heading'. Round 1's item (no figure check) is closed: the figure is checked and WRONG-FIGURE is a verdict. The housekeeper/house-steward finding is confirmed or corrected. The independent checker serves the asker's 'I wrote them, so I'm not the right one to check them'.

decisions.summary: Three comparative questions (servants' wages by post from the checked rows; income division and servants by income; provision and household-goods prices verbatim with units, unpriced named items SILENT), tagged subject=comparative,money; setting=city; level=counts-and-measurements; each opens with a comparative-yardstick intro
decisions.why: FR-006 item for item; the first question is the GM's own example 'what did a Regency English household pay its servants?'. Tags and intro carry FR-002.

decisions.summary: Comment on #2: per question the fragment file, verdicts, what is open; the extraction check per row; edition and page of each figure
decisions.why: FR-007 and the asker's 'Same answer format: fragment files, verdicts, what is still open' and 'Note the edition and page of each figure'.

decisions.summary: Order: vocabulary/build/test, guidelines/contract, source/archive, extraction check, questions write then check, implementation-check line, answer, report/done/land GATED
